correctness.rationale: Orthogonal distinct character rows give Parseval normalization. One coordinate-pair Walsh sum is 2(−1)^{αβ}, so the nonzero-frequency D-sum is −r(−1)^q/2 and the restricted Gram is ((r−1)I+S_E)/(2r). The triangle product on a rooted pair of differences is −(−1)^B. All four triangle products multiply to +1, and switching to normalize the edges at one root shows that triangle signs determine the class. Relabeling gives all-positive, exactly one negative edge, or all-negative representatives, according to 0, 2, or 4 negative triangles. In the one-negative-edge case the two pair differences give eigenvalues +1 and −1, and the pair-constant block [−1,2;2,1] gives ±√5. The two uniform-sign matrices give the other spectra. For the all-positive and all-negative types the nondegenerate symplectic equations give respectively n(n−1)(n/2)(n/4)/24 and n(n−1)(n/2−2)(n/4−3)/24 unordered masks; the remainder is the middle class. These classes are intrinsic to the triangle signs, so the root criteria are invariant. The retained lower frame bound is 1−λ_max(P_E); all-positive has strictly largest λ_max and all classes occur for n≥16. The only Gram singularity is at r=4 in the all-negative class, which does not impair the retained frame. The asserted m=2 and m=3 counts agree with exact substitution and the frozen outputs.
residual_risks: Finite output is corroboration at two dimensions, not the all-m proof. No assertion about arbitrary nonlinear bent frames or greater erasure sizes was checked.

evidence: In any regular two-graph on n vertices with a positive triangles per pair, let N_j count four-sets with j positive triangles. Counting triangle/four-set incidences gives 2N₂+4N₄=binom(n,2)a(n−3)/3; counting pairs of triangles along their common pair gives N₂+6N₄=binom(n,2)binom(a,2). Only j=0,2,4 are possible.
With a=n/2 these two equations and N₀+N₂+N₄=binom(n,4) give precisely the frozen masses N₄,N₂,N₀; positivity gives equality in the standard erasure bound and fixes its attainment count.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No family-specific incidence beyond standard two-graph regularity is needed. The census is a short algebraic specialization of these elementary moment counts and universal small signed matrices; the theorem's remaining local criteria and rank observations follow from switching and the resulting eigenvalues. Failure is based on this demonstrated implication, not an inaccessible possible prior source.

In fact the full sign matrix has eigenvalues 1±r from the known Parseval/equiangular parameters, so S²=2S+(n−1)I. Multiplying each off-diagonal entry of S² by the corresponding S entry gives the signed triangle excess 2 per pair and thus a=n/2, without a special quadratic computation.

value.rationale: Four-erasure stability of a natural frame is well motivated, but all identifying four-mask statistics here reduce to universal signed K4 matrices and two elementary incidence moments from already fixed frame parameters. No new family-specific invariant survives that reduction; the sharp worst bound is a specialization of a known general erasure result. A useful worked example is not a distinct scientific census at this threshold.
residual_risks: This does not discount higher-erasure or other questions for which two-graph regularity no longer determines the answer; no such theorem is supplied in the frozen record.
